unverified.heading: What we couldn't verify, and why it matters
unverified.intro: We marked these on the demo as yellow "to confirm" tags instead of guessing, because we won't put a claim on your site we can't back up. Your current pages disagree with each other on some of them, and a few have no number at all.

items.why: Your site says both "over 25 years" and "established 2011," and a homeowner who has been quoted three big jobs will notice a number that doesn't add up.
Someone who was told they need a new panel wants to look up the license before trusting the second opinion.
"Kansas and surrounding areas" doesn't tell a homeowner outside Wichita whether you'll come look.
Your site says a one-year warranty is available, but not what it covers, and a wary homeowner will ask.

unverified.closing: This is what our onboarding call nails down. Fifteen minutes, and every tag becomes a real, true line.

why: Your header says “Serving the State of Kansas” on every page, and your homepage headline is “Electrician Services.” A Wichita homeowner with a dead outlet, and Google, can't tell that you're the electrician on N Pennsylvania Ave.

Your customers already describe the electrician you are. Bruce P.: “John took time to examine the problem and determined that current set up was safe and nothing was needed.” Jennifer B.: “They saved me a service call.” Today those words sit on Google, while your site's “Write a Review” button opens a private Hibu survey.
So the demo tells one story everywhere: you look first and say so. It opens with Electrician in Wichita, KS, and gives electrical repair and panel upgrades a page each.

confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your homepage, Our Team and FAQ pages say over 25 years, while your About page says Year Established 2011, so which number should every listing use?
Your site shows no street address, while your Google listing puts you at 232 N Pennsylvania Ave and a BBB search result shows 1424 N Mosley St, so which address should every listing use?
Your header and footer say “the State of Kansas” and “Kansas and surrounding areas,” while your FAQ says Wichita and the surrounding areas, so which towns should Google list as your service area?

lead.heading: Why we led with looking first
lead.text: Google can find “fast, friendly, licensed” on any electrician’s site. It can’t find what your customers wrote: Bruce P. was told his meter needed nothing, and Jennifer B. was sent to Evergy first. A lead built on real reviews like those gives Google something only Bybee has.
